questions.q: What are the three core pieces of Setup Home identified in this lesson?
options: Chatter, Files, and Notes
The App Launcher, Reports, and Dashboards
Only a single search box, with no other navigation elements
Quick Find, the Home/Object Manager tabs, and Search Setup
questions.explain: Setup Home's three core pieces, per this lesson, are Quick Find, the Home/Object Manager tabs, and the Search Setup box.

questions.q: What is the difference between the grid icon and the gear icon in the Salesforce header, per this lesson?
options: They both open the exact same Setup page
The grid icon opens the App Launcher; the gear icon opens Setup
Neither icon has any function in Lightning Experience
The grid icon opens Setup; the gear icon opens the App Launcher
questions.explain: The grid icon opens the App Launcher for switching apps/records, while the gear icon is what actually opens Setup — a common early mix-up.

questions.q: What happens when you type into the Quick Find box in Setup, according to this lesson?
options: It logs you out of the current org
It opens a new browser tab
The entire left sidebar filters live to match what you've typed
Nothing happens until you press a separate Search button
questions.explain: Quick Find filters the Setup sidebar live as you type, narrowing it to matching pages immediately.

questions.q: What two broad sections does this lesson say the Setup sidebar is split into?
options: Administration and Platform Tools
Classic and Lightning
Reports and Dashboards
Sales and Service
questions.explain: The Setup sidebar is broadly organized into Administration (Users, Data, Email) and Platform Tools (Apps, Objects, Automation).

questions.q: Why does Object Manager get its own top-level tab instead of living in the sidebar, per this lesson?
options: Because admins open it so frequently that it's pulled out for quicker access
Because it is only accessible to System Administrators, never other profiles
Because it is not actually part of Setup at all
Because Salesforce is removing Object Manager in the next release
questions.explain: Object Manager is deliberately pulled into its own top-level tab next to Home because it's opened so frequently.
